$comment: v2 budgets from docs/v2/architecture.md §3.7. Bytes, gzip level 9, per file as the browser downloads it (fonts: file bytes). Checked by npm run check:budget. Component budgets are measured in the custom-elements build (module + import closure, excluding the runtime). Only tags in "enforce" (rebuilt for v2) fail the check; family agents add theirs when they finish. Others are reported as pending.
$globalCssComment: R23 (amends W7, approved 22 October 2026): sc.css 10 KiB gzip, from 9 KiB. sc-footer and sc-breadcrumbs became CSS only (their rules moved into sc.css, about 0.8 KiB), and sc-callout, sc-status-tag, sc-tile and sc-channel-network gained pre-upgrade reservations, in exchange for about 6 KiB less JavaScript on every page with a footer and breadcrumbs.
$componentsComment: Overrides of componentGzip. sc-button: 5 KiB, because its closure counts the shared locale controller (1.0 KiB) in full; its icons (the named set and the spinner, Material Symbols) are inlined into its own module. See specs/sc-button.md.

components.$chromeComment: Site chrome (C1): each closure counts shared chunks in full that a channel page pays once: the locale controller (0.9 KiB), the chrome icon set (1.1 KiB), the channel names from common.ts and the descriptors (1.0 KiB) and the disclosure and motion helpers (1.2 KiB). Each component's own module is 1.7 to 4.4 KiB. See each spec's Budget section.
components.$navComment: sc-bottom-nav 4.5 KiB, the same as sc-account-nav (W8): both take any of the eight destination icons by name (data-icon), and the Material Symbols set needs an Outlined and a Filled path for each (ICN-02: the current item is Filled), about 1.3 KiB inlined. Approved (W14). Both raised by 64 B to 4,672 B (W14a): the Linux CI build compresses about 30 B larger than macOS.

$c4Comment: sc-modal 7 KiB: a dialog that is also a bottom sheet with drag, focus return and the session-timeout countdown with plural announcements; its own module is 4.7 KiB plus the same two shared chunks. See specs/sc-step-progress.md and specs/sc-modal.md.
$pageCssComment: Approved (W13): 4 KiB, from 3 KiB. The typical page parses the stylesheets of 9 components (sc-search renders sc-button): 3,914 B gzip once Stencil's minifier failure is fixed (scripts/lib/minify-css.cjs; it was 4,281 B). Type roles are already shared tokens; what remains is each component's own layout, states, forced-colours and RTL rules. The largest are sc-button (1.3 KiB, six variants and the loading state) and sc-footer (1.1 KiB, both variants). 3 KiB would mean dropping states or variants.
$siteComment: Documentation site (scripts/build-site.mjs), checked by npm run check:site-budget: every built page against pageJsGzip and pageComponentCssGzip (custom-elements modules it imports, plus site.js), plus the site's own files below. A component's showcase page may exceed the page budgets by the approved overrides above componentGzip of the components it demonstrates.
$siteFontsComment: site.pageFontsMixedBytes (110 KiB, approved R18): a page that sets text in both scripts, such as an Arabic page around an English document or an English component page with Arabic examples, downloads the Arabic and the Latin faces it uses. Single-script pages keep pageFontsEnBytes and pageFontsArBytes. Checked by npm run check:site-a11y.
$siteChromeComment: R21 (approved, decisions.md on v2, 845e937): documentation-site pages may also use the approved overrides above componentGzip of the site chrome they carry (site.chromeTags: sc-site-header +3.5 KiB). Tightened by v2-lib-gaps: sc-footer (+2 KiB) left the list when it and sc-breadcrumbs became CSS only and stopped costing JavaScript. R22 (approved): on component pages sc-channel-switcher is showcase tooling and counts at its full approved budget (site.showcaseTooling); on /search/ sc-search is the page's own component and brings its approved override (site.pageComponents). Documentation site only: service pages keep the plain page budgets. Enforced by npm run check:site-budget.
